APPLE’S $2,000 FOLDABLE IPHONE COULD SELL 6 MILLION UNITS  Apple’s rumored first foldable iPhone, expected to cost around $2,000, could reportedly sell as many as 6 million units. The device is expected to bring Apple’s design, software, and premium ecosystem to the foldable-phone market, where high prices and durability concerns have limited mass adoption.  If Apple can deliver a polished foldable experience, the product could become a major new category for the iPhone lineup despite its premium price. The projected 6 million sales would also signal strong consumer interest in Apple’s entry into foldable smartphones, potentially intensifying competition across the high-end mobile market. (@FirstSquaw)

U.S. INFLATION BREADTH SHOWS SIGNS OF COOLING  Despite softer core PCE revisions, 51% of the PCE basket is still rising at 3% or more annually, little changed from recent months.  However, the share experiencing inflation above 3% on a six-month annualized basis fell to 44% in August, from 49% in July — its lowest since October 2025.  Underlying price pressures are easing, although inflation remains widespread. (@WalterBloomberg)

It's officially Fed day.  We expect a "hawkish pause" today.  The Fed will hold interest rates unchanged but lay the groundwork for a December rate hike, bringing total rate hikes in 2026 to +50 basis points.  Why?  Because the US economy is now facing both supply-side and rising demand-side inflationary pressures, while the labor market continues to weaken beneath the surface.  This puts the Fed in an increasingly difficult position: Inflation is demanding tighter monetary policy, while underlying labor market weakness is calling for the opposite.  We expect the Fed to prioritize inflation today, keeping the door open for further tightening in December. (@TheKobeissiLetter)
